findings.text: _restore_move_journal re-implements the restore that recover_project_state_transactions already performs in the same module (:2211-2241): the same journal parse and _safe_segment ids, the same base64 decode with validate=True, and the same resource_path plus mkdir plus write_atomically(mode=0o600, fsync, fsync_directory, binary=True) loop. The two copies can drift about what a valid journal and a valid restore are, and extracting one primitive would let both callers share it.

_assert_reply_matches_disk compares sprint_versions only in the applied branch (:153). On every not-applied step (four of the six cases plus the read-back case) the reply's versions are never compared against a fresh read, and the refusal branches at reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1750 and :1760 emit no versions to compare, so the done_when's 'verdict and versions match a fresh read' is measured only where the move landed.

The population arm ran 27 test files, but 31 tests/*.py files import reckon.project_state; this one and seven others (test_a_cold_read_parses_each_plan_once, test_cleared_hold_releases_a_blocked_plan, test_dispatch_reads_derivations_cheaply, test_graph_target_reads_one_readiness, test_held_blocker_probe, test_the_served_count_and_the_orphan_rule_read_the_assembly, test_timestamp_callers_batch_b) are absent from population-head.log, so the done_when's stated population is not fully measured at either arm.
